question: A 60-year-old man has had intermittent pain in his right great toe for the past 2 years. Joint aspiration and crystal analysis shows thin, tapered, needle shaped intracellular crystals that are strongly negatively birefringent. Radiograph demonstrates joint space narrowing of the 1st metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint with medial soft tissue swelling. What is the most likely cause of this condition?
analysis: The clinical presentation of intermittent pain in the right great toe, along with joint aspiration findings of thin, tapered, needle-shaped intracellular crystals that are strongly negatively birefringent, and radiographic evidence of joint space narrowing of the 1st metatarsophalangeal joint with soft tissue swelling, is highly suggestive of gout. Gout is characterized by monosodium urate crystal deposition in the joints, leading to inflammation and symptoms like those described in the case.
